title: Net-Ev$^2$: A Generative Simulator for Network Event Evolution

problem.claim: Simulating how disturbance events propagate their impacts across real-world networks is a challenging task.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not jointly model structured attributes and unstructured event semantics while capturing network topology in network event evolution simulations.

contributions.claim: Net-Ev$^2$ is a generative simulator that jointly leverages event cues while preserving network topology in simulations.
The framework uses structure-guided masked pre-training and a topology-aware diffusion process with U-Net-like graph downsampling and upsampling during denoising.
The work introduces Net-Ev$^2$-6.5M, a multimodal benchmark of aligned event and network traffic data across four large-scale road networks, and the JL-MMD topology-aware metric.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Net-Ev$^2$ as a novel generative simulator.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance and strong generalization ability in extensive experiments.
The authors report that code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative simulators aim to reduce real-world trial and error by modeling future-state evolution.
The paper focuses on simulating the propagation of disturbance-event impacts across real-world networks.
Existing approaches are described as insufficient for combining event attributes and semantics with network topology.
Net-Ev$^2$ combines event cues with topology preservation through structure-guided pre-training and topology-aware diffusion.
The work adds a benchmark and metric, reports extensive experiments, and provides code.

source_observation.claim: The simulator can generate simulations from natural-language event input only at inference time.

interpretation.claim: Natural-language conditioning may reduce the interface burden for practical simulation use.

application.claim: A simulation workflow could expose event specification through natural-language inputs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how reliably natural-language inputs cover different event types or operational settings.

source_observation.claim: The work evaluates topological fidelity with a dedicated topology-aware metric and a benchmark spanning four large-scale road networks.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation of network-event simulators should include both aligned multimodal data and topology-sensitive measures.

application.claim: A network-dynamics evaluation pipeline could pair domain-aligned data with topology-aware metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the metric construction, benchmark composition, or transfer conditions beyond the four road networks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the experimental baselines, quantitative results, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not detail the model architecture, training data construction, or generalization settings.
